overview.headline: Constant speed flight and how distance relates to ground speed and time

keyPoints.point: Aircraft in level flight with lift equal to weight and thrust equal to drag can hold constant speed
keyPoints.quote: an airplane can maintain a constant speed and level flight, in which the lift is equal to the weight, and the thrust is equal to the drag.

keyPoints.point: With no net external force aircraft keeps constant airspeed described by Newton’s First Law of Motion
keyPoints.quote: Since there is no net external force on the aircraft, the aircraft maintains a constant airspeed as described by Newton’s First Law of Motion.

keyPoints.point: Ground speed stays constant while wind speed stays steady for a cruising aircraft
keyPoints.quote: The ground speed remains constant as long as the wind speed is constant.

keyPoints.point: Maximum distance aircraft can fly equals ground speed times maximum time
keyPoints.quote: The maximum distance that the aircraft can fly is then equal to the ground speed times the maximum time (tmax).

keyTerms.gloss: speed of aircraft relative to ground influenced by wind and constant in example
keyTerms.quote: The ground speed remains constant as long as the wind speed is constant.

keyTerms.gloss: farthest distance aircraft can fly given maximum time at constant ground speed
keyTerms.quote: We call this distance the maximum range (R) of the aircraft.
